title: SQL filters, functions and autoescape
description:
SQL in templates: filters and functions that write SQL for the panel's database, and
`query.autoescape`. See `:help dbdash-template-filters`.

show.title: SQL filters and functions (the SQL they write)
show.description:
The filters and functions that write SQL for the panel's database (SQLite here):
literals (`sql_quote`, `sql_escape`), lists (`sql_in`), identifiers (`sql_id`),
LIMIT values (`sql_limit`), `sql_case()` and `sql_concat()`. Each row is a
template as written and the SQL it gave.

query.sql:
-- query.autoescape: every value written with {% raw %}{{ }}{% endraw %} is a literal of the database; SQL from
-- the filters, | safe, macros and dbdash.safe() is not escaped again.
WITH t(name) AS (VALUES ('O''Neil'))
SELECT {{ args.name }} AS arg,
       {{ args.depts | length }} AS depts,
       {{ 'name' | safe }} = {{ args.name }} AS same,
       {% autoescape false %}'{{ args.limit }}'{% endautoescape %} AS autoescape_off,
       {% lua %}return dbdash.safe("upper(name)"){% endlua %} AS from_lua
FROM t

show.title: query.autoescape: true
show.description:
With `query.autoescape: true` every {% raw %}`{{ value }}`{% endraw %} is a literal; filters, `| safe`,
macros and `dbdash.safe()` are not escaped again, and {% raw %}`{% autoescape false %}`{% endraw %} turns it
off for a part.

show.title: a query with the filters
show.description:
Without autoescape values go in as written: quote them with `sql_in`, `sql_quote`,
`sql_id` and `sql_limit`.
